plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following constitutional amendments paved the way for the introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
plain.explanation: The 101st Constitution Amendment Act, 2016 inserted Article 246A, empowering the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to GST. This landmark amendment fundamentally restructured India's indirect tax framework.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Article 279A of the Constitution of India, who is the Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
options: Union Minister of State for Finance
Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
plain.explanation: Article 279A mandates the constitution of the GST Council by the President. The Union Finance Minister acts as the Chairperson of the GST Council, while the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance is a member.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following items is currently NOT subsumed under GST and continues to be taxed under the pre-GST central excise and state VAT regime?
plain.explanation: Petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) have been temporarily excluded from GST. The GST Council will decide the date from which GST will be levied on these petroleum products.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the primary voting weight allocated to the Central Government and the State Governments combined in the decisions of the GST Council?
options: Center has 1/3rd weight and States have 2/3rd weight combined
Center has 1/2 weight and States have 1/2 weight combined
Center has 2/3rd weight and States have 1/3rd weight combined
Center has 3/4th weight and States have 1/4th weight combined
plain.explanation: According to Article 279A, the vote of the Central Government has a weight of one-third of the total votes cast, and the votes of all the State Governments taken together have a weight of two-thirds of the total votes cast in that meeting.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following taxes levied by the Central Government was NOT subsumed into GST?
options: Additional Excise Duty (Goods of Special Importance)
plain.explanation: Basic Customs Duty (BCD) is levied on goods imported into India under the Customs Act, 1962, and has not been subsumed under GST. Central Excise, Service Tax, and Additional Excise Duties were subsumed.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: GST is a destination-based consumption tax. What does this fundamentally imply regarding tax revenue collection?
options: Tax revenue accrues to the state where the manufacturing unit is located
Tax revenue accrues to the state where the goods or services are consumed
Tax revenue is retained entirely by the Central Government
Tax revenue is distributed equally among all states regardless of consumption
plain.explanation: GST is a destination-based tax, meaning the tax revenue goes to the state where the final consumption takes place, unlike origin-based taxes which favoured manufacturing states.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under the dual GST model implemented in India, intra-state supplies attract which of the following combinations of taxes?
plain.explanation: In an intra-state supply of goods or services, both Central GST (CGST) and State GST (SGST) or Union Territory GST (UTGST) are levied concurrently on the same taxable value.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which article of the Constitution of India defines 'Goods and Services Tax' as any tax on supply of goods, or services or both except taxes on the supply of the alcoholic liquor for human consumption?
plain.explanation: Article 366(12A) of the Constitution of India defines GST as 'any tax on supply of goods, or services or both except taxes on the supply of the alcoholic liquor for human consumption'.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What majority is required for taking any decision in the GST Council?
options: Simple majority of members present and voting
Not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting
Two-thirds majority of all members of the council
plain.explanation: Every decision of the GST Council must be taken at a meeting by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following authorities administers the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) on inter-state supplies and imports?
options: Both Central and State Governments in a 50:50 ratio
plain.explanation: IGST is levied and collected by the Central Government under the IGST Act, and the tax is subsequently apportioned between the Centre and the consuming State as per the recommendations of the GST Council.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Why was the 'additional tax of up to 1% on inter-state supply of goods' proposed during the conceptual stages of GST ultimately dropped?
options: It violated the fundamental destination-based nature of GST and caused cascading effects
It generated too much revenue for the Centre
It was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court prior to enactment
plain.explanation: The proposed 1% additional tax on inter-state supplies was dropped because it violated the fundamental destination-based principle of GST, acted as a cascading tax (origin-based), and created economic distortions.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which Constitutional provision prohibits any tax to be levied or collected except by authority of law?
plain.explanation: Article 265 of the Constitution of India lays down that 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law', which forms the foundational bedrock for all tax legislation, including GST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following taxes levied by State Governments was NOT subsumed into GST?
plain.explanation: Stamp duty levied on immovable property transactions has not been subsumed under GST. State VAT, entertainment tax, and luxury tax levied by states were successfully subsumed.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In the context of GST, what does the acronym SGST stand for?
plain.explanation: SGST stands for State Goods and Services Tax, levied by individual state governments on intra-state supplies under respective State GST Acts.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: How does GST eliminate the cascading effect of taxes (tax on tax)?
options: By offering exemptions to all small businesses
By providing seamless Input Tax Credit (ITC) across the supply chain
By fixing a uniform tax rate of 18% on all goods and services
By collecting tax only at the retail level
plain.explanation: GST eliminates the cascading effect by allowing registered taxable persons to claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) for taxes paid on inputs at each stage of the supply chain, ensuring tax is paid only on the value added.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which specific constitutional article empowers Parliament to make laws with respect to GST while granting concurrent powers to State Legislatures?
plain.explanation: Article 246A (introduced by the 101st Amendment) gives both Parliament and State Legislatures the power to make laws with respect to GST imposed by the Union or by the State respectively.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the status of 'alcoholic liquor for human consumption' under the GST framework?
options: Taxable at the highest GST slab of 28% plus cess
Completely outside the purview of GST; continues to be taxed by states
Exempted from all forms of taxation
plain.explanation: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is completely kept outside the constitutional definition and purview of GST. States retain the exclusive power to levy excise duty and sales tax/VAT on it.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution was amended to accommodate GST?
options: Both List I (Union List) and List II (State List)
plain.explanation: The Seventh Schedule was amended: entries in List I (Union List) and List II (State List) were modified (e.g., Entry 92 and 92C of Union List deleted; Entry 54 of State List modified) to enable dual GST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under GST law, what is the nomenclature used for supplies made within the same Union Territory without a legislature?
plain.explanation: For intra-UT supplies in Union Territories without a legislature (like Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep), CGST and UTGST (Union Territory Goods and Services Tax) are levied concurrently.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following taxes levied by local bodies (such as municipalities) was subsumed into GST?
plain.explanation: Octroi and Entry Tax levied by local bodies were subsumed into GST. Property tax, professional tax, and local parking taxes remain outside GST and continue to be levied by local authorities.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What was the primary legislative objective behind enacting the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017?
options: To provide permanent financial grants to underdeveloped states
To compensate states for any revenue loss arising due to the implementation of GST for a transition period
To fund infrastructure projects in union territories
To compensate central government for losses incurred in inter-state trade
plain.explanation: The GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 was enacted to provide compensation to states for loss of revenue arising on account of implementation of GST for a transition period (originally 5 years) funded via a cess on luxury and demerit goods.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which constitutional article places restrictions on the imposition of tax on the sale or purchase of goods in the course of inter-state trade or commerce?
plain.explanation: Article 286 of the Constitution imposes restrictions on imposition of tax on the sale or purchase of goods in the course of inter-state trade or commerce, which led to the formulation of IGST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the role of the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN)?
options: To adjudicate tax disputes between taxpayers and the department
To provide the IT infrastructure and services to central and state governments, taxpayers, and other stakeholders
To formulate tax rates and exemption policies
To audit all registered taxpayers annually
plain.explanation: GSTN is a non-profit, non-government company providing the robust IT backbone and shared IT infrastructure for registration, return filing, tax payments, and matching of invoices under GST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following best describes the tax structure of GST regarding multiple rate slabs?
options: Single flat rate across all goods and services
Multiple rate slabs (e.g., 0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%) along with a compensation cess on specified goods
Regressive rate structure decreasing with higher transaction value
Discretionary rates decided by individual states
plain.explanation: India has adopted a multi-rate GST structure with standard slabs of 0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%, supplemented by a compensation cess on luxury, sin, and demerit goods.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which authority is empowered to make recommendations on GST rates, exemption lists, and threshold limits under Article 279A?
options: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council)
plain.explanation: Article 279A empowers the GST Council to make recommendations to the Union and States on GST rates, exemptions, threshold limits, model GST laws, etc.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a supplier registered in Maharashtra charge IGST on the supply of goods to a buyer located within Maharashtra?
options: Yes, if the buyer requests an inter-state invoice
No, because a supply within the same state is an intra-state supply attracting CGST and SGST
Yes, if the goods originated outside Maharashtra
Yes, at the discretion of the supplier
plain.explanation: When both the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in the same state, it constitutes an intra-state supply, which mandatorily attracts CGST and SGST/UTGST, not IGST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following constitutional provisions guarantees freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India, subject to public interest restrictions?
plain.explanation: Article 301 of the Constitution states that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, which necessitated careful structuring of IGST to prevent trade barriers between states.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under the pre-GST indirect tax regime, what was the primary cause of the 'cascading effect'?
options: Non-availability of cross-credit between Central taxes (like Excise) and State taxes (like VAT)
Uniform tax rates across all states
Exemption of small traders from taxation
plain.explanation: The cascading effect occurred because Central taxes paid on inputs could not be set off against State taxes output liabilities (and vice versa), leading to tax being levied on tax.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following entities functions as the apex operational body for administering central indirect tax laws including GST at the national level?
options: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
plain.explanation: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) under the Ministry of Finance administers central indirect tax laws, including CGST, IGST, and Customs.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In the context of petroleum and natural gas, when can the GST Council notify the levy of GST on crude oil and high-speed diesel?
options: Automatically after 10 years from GST rollout
Only upon the recommendation of the GST Council
By a direct executive order of the Prime Minister
After ratification by all 28 states unconditionally
plain.explanation: As per Article 246A and related constitutional provisions, GST on petroleum crude, HSD, petrol, natural gas, and ATF will be levied from a date to be recommended by the GST Council.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd., located in the State of Gujarat, procures raw materials worth Rs. 10,00,000 from local suppliers within Gujarat and pays CGST and SGST. It also imports specialized machinery from Germany, paying Basic Customs Duty and IGST. The company manufactures finished goods and sells 60% of its production to buyers in Maharashtra and 40% to buyers within Gujarat.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What type of tax will M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. charge on the sale of goods made to buyers located in Maharashtra?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Since the location of the supplier is in Gujarat and the place of supply (buyer) is in Maharashtra, it is an inter-state supply, which attracts Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What type of tax will M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. charge on the sale of goods made to buyers located within Gujarat?
linkedMcqs.explanation: When both the supplier and the buyer are located within the same state (Gujarat), it is an intra-state supply, attracting CGST and SGST concurrently.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can M/s Apex Manufacturing Ltd. utilize the IGST paid on the import of machinery against the CGST/SGST liability arising on intra-state sales?
options: No, import IGST cannot be utilized for domestic supplies
Yes, IGST credit can be utilized against CGST and SGST liability in the prescribed order
Yes, but only against SGST and never against CGST
No, import duties cannot be set off under GST
linkedMcqs.explanation: Input Tax Credit (ITC) of IGST paid on imports is seamlessly integrated into the GST credit pool and can be utilized against CGST and SGST liabilities after utilizing available IGST liability first.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which constitutional principle ensures that the revenue from the IGST charged on sales to Maharashtra eventually benefits the consuming state?
linkedMcqs.explanation: GST is a destination-based consumption tax; hence, the IGST collected on inter-state sales is apportioned to the consuming state where the goods are finally consumed.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: The State of Zeta has recently witnessed a sharp decline in its state tax revenues following the nationwide rollout of GST. The state finance minister raises concerns in a GST Council meeting regarding budgetary shortfalls. Simultaneously, the Council discusses whether to bring electricity and alcoholic liquor for human consumption under the GST net, and whether to revise the compensation cess rates on luxury vehicles.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What constitutional mechanism was originally established to protect states like Zeta from revenue shortfalls during the initial years of GST?
options: Permanent special grants from the RBI
GST Compensation to States Act providing guaranteed revenue growth backed by a compensation cess
Automatic borrowing rights from international banks
linkedMcqs.explanation: The GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 guaranteed states a 14% protected revenue growth for a transition period, funded through a compensation cess levied on luxury and demerit goods.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can the GST Council unilaterally bring 'alcoholic liquor for human consumption' under GST without a constitutional amendment?
options: Yes, by a three-fourths majority vote in the GST Council
No, because the Constitution explicitly excludes alcoholic liquor from the definition of GST under Article 366(12A)
Yes, if all Union Territories agree
Yes, through an executive notification issued by the Ministry of Finance
linkedMcqs.explanation: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is excluded by definition in Article 366(12A). Bringing it under GST requires a formal constitutional amendment passed by Parliament and ratified by states.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What voting majority is required in the GST Council for decisions regarding changes in compensation cess or tax rates?
options: Not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting
Two-thirds majority of central members only
linkedMcqs.explanation: All decisions of the GST Council, including rates, exemptions, and cesses, must be taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the status of electricity under the GST framework?
options: Taxed at a special merit rate of 5%
Exempted under GST while continuing to be governed by state electricity duties and pre-GST laws
Taxed under IGST for inter-state transmission
linkedMcqs.explanation: Electricity is neither subsumed into GST nor taxed under GST currently; it continues to be governed by pre-GST laws and state-level electricity duties.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: A multi-national enterprise, Global Tech Corp, provides IT-enabled consultancy services from its office in Bengaluru to a client in Chennai. In the same tax period, Global Tech Corp also procures office stationery locally in Bengaluru, paying CGST and SGST, and avails cloud computing services from a server hosted in Mumbai, paying IGST.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What category of supply is the consultancy service provided by Global Tech Corp from Bengaluru to the client in Chennai?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Since the location of the supplier (Bengaluru, Karnataka) and the place of supply (Chennai, Tamil Nadu) are in two different states, it is an inter-state supply attracting IGST.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How should Global Tech Corp treat the CGST and SGST paid on local procurement of office stationery?
options: Claim it as an expense in the Profit and Loss account
Claim it as Input Tax Credit (ITC) to set off against its output tax liabilities
Claim a refund directly from the State Government treasury
linkedMcqs.explanation: Taxes paid on local procurements used in the course or furtherance of business qualify as Input Tax Credit (ITC) and can be utilized to offset output tax liabilities, preventing cascading.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which tax will be levied on the cloud computing service procured from Mumbai by the Bengaluru office?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Supply of services between Mumbai (Maharashtra) and Bengaluru (Karnataka) is an inter-state supply of services, which attracts Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which legislative enactment governs the levy of IGST on inter-state supply of services in India?
linkedMcqs.explanation: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (IGST Act) governs the levy and collection of IGST on all inter-state supplies of goods and services and on imports into India.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: A legislative drafting committee is reviewing the historical evolution of indirect taxes in India to prepare a training module for CA Intermediate students. The committee is analyzing why certain taxes like Central Excise Duty and State VAT were replaced, why Customs Duty was retained, and how the dual GST structure was embedded into the Constitution through specific legislative entries.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Why was Basic Customs Duty retained outside the GST framework?
options: Because customs duties are exclusively levied on domestic consumption within states
Because customs duty protects domestic industry from foreign competition and is levied on goods entering India from outside the country, separate from domestic supply
Because the Constitution prohibits merging customs with GST
Because international trade agreements forbid subsuming customs duties
linkedMcqs.explanation: Basic Customs Duty is levied on imports from foreign territories under the Customs Act to regulate foreign trade and protect domestic industry, and is distinct from domestic supplies taxed under GST.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which entry in the Union List (List I of the Seventh Schedule) was amended or deleted to accommodate the taxation of services under GST?
options: Entry 92 (Taxes on sale or purchase of newspapers)
Entry 54 (Taxes on sale or purchase of goods)
linkedMcqs.explanation: Entry 92C of the Union List, which earlier dealt with 'Taxes on services', was deleted by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, as services are now taxed under Article 246A via CGST and IGST.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What primary economic defect of the pre-GST regime was addressed by the introduction of the dual GST model?
options: High compliance cost for large enterprises
Cascading effect of taxes due to lack of seamless input tax credit across central and state levies
Excessive collection of direct income taxes
linkedMcqs.explanation: The dual GST model eliminated the cascading effect by allowing cross-utilization of CGST and SGST (or seamless IGST credit), ensuring tax is levied only on value addition.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under the dual GST framework, if a state enacts a State GST law, what is the mandatory constitutional prerequisite regarding conformity with model laws?
options: State laws must be identical to Central law in all substantive matters recommended by the GST Council
State GST laws can have completely independent tax rate slabs and exemption limits
State GST laws require prior presidential assent before draft preparation
State GST laws apply only to manufacturing sectors
linkedMcqs.explanation: While SGST laws are enacted by respective state legislatures, they generally conform to the Model SGST Act recommended by the GST Council to maintain uniformity in definitions, procedures, and tax incidence across India.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Zenith Enterprises operates a chain of retail stores across multiple states and Union Territories, including Delhi (UT with legislature), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (UT without legislature), and Uttar Pradesh. The company transfers goods inter-branch, makes retail sales to consumers, and procures taxable services from local consultants.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: For retail sales made from a store in Andaman and Nicobar Islands to a local customer, which taxes will Zenith Enterprises charge?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Andaman and Nicobar Islands is a Union Territory without a legislature. Intra-UT supplies in such territories attract CGST and UTGST concurrently.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: For retail sales made from a store in Delhi to a local customer, which taxes will Zenith Enterprises charge?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Delhi is a Union Territory with its own legislature (treated as a State for GST purposes). Intra-state/intra-UT supplies in Delhi attract CGST and SGST concurrently.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal status of UTGST under the GST legislative framework?
options: It is levied under the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 for UTs without legislatures
It is a state tax levied by neighboring state governments
It is an optional tax levied by municipal corporations
It replaces IGST for all domestic transactions
linkedMcqs.explanation: UTGST is levied under the UTGST Act, 2017 in Union Territories without a legislature (such as Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Ladakh).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Zenith Enterprises transfers goods from its warehouse in Uttar Pradesh to its retail branch in Delhi, how is this transaction treated under GST?
options: Not a supply since it is between branches of the same entity
Deemed supply of goods between distinct persons, attracting IGST
Exempted from all taxes as internal stock transfer
Subject to CGST and SGST of Uttar Pradesh only
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 7 read with Schedule I of the CGST Act, supply of goods between different establishments of the same person having separate registrations (in different states/UTs) is treated as a supply ('distinct persons') and attracts IGST.
